drhp.business: IRIS builds software platforms that convert regulatory compliance and corporate disclosure into structured, machine-readable and increasingly AI-assisted processes. The business is organised across SupTech (digital reporting, data collection, validation and supervisory technology for regulators and public authorities), RegTech (disclosure management, sustainability and structured financial reporting for enterprises, led by the IRIS Carbon platform) and DataTech. Following the strategic divestment of its TaxTech / GST ASP business, the Company is focused on a scalable, product-led model with …

drhp.expansion: IRIS is an asset-light software products business, so its expansion is expressed as product build-out, market entry and talent rather than plant or capacity projects; the annual report contains no plant, line or capacity commissioning programme. drhp.one_liner: IRIS RegTech Solutions Limited (formerly IRIS Business Services Limited) is a product-led regulatory technology company operating at the intersection of regulation, reporting and technology, serving regulators through SupTech and enterprises through RegTech and DataTech platforms.

risks.note: Many large financial institutions and supervisory authorities still run fragmented legacy systems, making deployment of modern compliance platforms operationally complex and resource intensive; the report states these integration challenges often impact implementation timelines, interoperability and enterprise-wide scalability - directly affecting revenue recognition timing and project cost for a platform vendor.
risks.risk: Integration with fragmented legacy infrastructure at customers and regulators

risks.note: Inconsistent data quality, fragmented information systems and multi-jurisdictional reporting misalignment are flagged as persistent industry problems that can impact reporting accuracy, automation efficiency and regulatory responsiveness - the exact outcomes IRIS platforms are bought to deliver.
risks.risk: Data quality and interoperability across multi-jurisdiction reporting

risks.note: As AI is embedded into compliance workflows, regulators and enterprises are emphasising auditable, explainable and traceable systems, particularly in high-risk workflows where automated decisions require clear accountability; this raises the product and assurance bar for an AI-led roadmap.

The Board's Report states operating margins moderated versus the prior year mainly due to continued investments in product development, technology, infrastructure, sales and marketing, and talent acquisition to support long-term growth - so revenue growth is not currently translating into operating leverage.
risks.risk: Margin moderation from a sustained investment phase

risks.note: The Board explicitly cautions that the gain on disposal of the TaxTech / GST ASP business is non-recurring in nature and that the Company's underlying operating performance should be viewed separately from the one-time impact of the divestment.
risks.risk: Earnings quality distorted by a one-time divestment gain

risks.note: Exports contributed 81% of total turnover in FY26 and the client base spans 55 countries, with international delivery through subsidiaries in the USA, Singapore, Malaysia and Italy - concentrating the business in cross-border regulatory cycles, currency movements and foreign procurement decisions.

IRIS handles regulatory and disclosure data for regulators, banks and corporates in an environment the report describes as facing rising cyber threats, data breaches and tightening data-governance regimes such as the DPDP Act; the Company mitigates through ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type II certifications, but a security failure would be reputationally decisive for a compliance vendor.
risks.risk: Data security and privacy obligations on sensitive regulatory data

risks.note: This is the Company's first BRSR, published voluntarily, with several practices described as remaining partial rather than fully operational, Scope 3 emissions based on spend-based estimates, and no external assurance obtained - leaving disclosure quality dependent on future build-out as ESG reporting obligations widen.
risks.risk: Early-stage ESG data and governance maturity

sk.overview: Broadcasting and streaming is a segment of the global media & entertainment (M&E) industry undergoing a structural shift to a 'new video economy' - the transition from traditional cable/DTH to internet-delivered video (OTT, FAST, CTV). The shift is characterised by fragmentation of viewership, globalisation of content, and a move to ad-supported models, and it is driving M&E companies to adopt cloud-native, purpose-built streaming-video software for production, preparation, distribution and monetization.
